title: Nancy Mace addresses religious persecution, crime case and Beaufort County shooting in new posts - Berkeley Leader
text:
U.S. Representative Nancy Mace, who serves South Carolina’s 1st district, posted a series of statements on October 15, 2025, addressing issues ranging from religious persecution to local law enforcement and a recent shooting in Beaufort County.
In her first post on October 15 at 14:33 UTC, Mace wrote, “Bill Maher said what the media refuses to: faith is under fire. You don’t have to be a Christian to see evil for what it is. What’s happening to Christians in Nigeria is genocide, and pretending it isn’t happening won’t make it stop.”
Later that day at 15:27 UTC, she commented on a criminal case involving an undocumented immigrant: “A Mexican national deported three times was arrested after being found with hundreds of images of child sexual abuse. Charleston County deputies led the effort to bring him to justice. LAW AND ORDER is back under President Trump. Predators will find no mercy.”
At 16:35 UTC on the same day, Mace addressed the aftermath of a violent incident in her state: “We’re praying for the victims of the Beaufort County shooting, the 20 injured and the four lives lost. Kashawn Glaze, 22, of Beaufort; Chiraad Smalls, 33, also of Beaufort; A’shan’tek Milledge, 22, of Burton; and Amos Gary, 54, of St. Helena. May they rest in peace, and may”
Mace has represented South Carolina’s 1st District in Congress since 2021 after succeeding Joe Cunningham. She previously served in the South Carolina House of Representatives from 2018 to 2020 and resides in Charleston. Born in Fort Bragg, North Carolina in 1977, she graduated from The Citadel in 1999 with a Bachelor of Science degree.
